answer: Each new identity first seals 8 GB of pseudo-random RAM offsets under a time-locked seed, then the verifier walks a falcon-quick sequential chain of cache-line traversals, demanding each line be touched in the order the seed dictates, like tracing a comet's tail through a mesa of memory banks without skipping a rock. Any out-of-order access breaks the seal, the probe fails, and the identity is rejected before earning stake. Forging 10000 sockpuppets means committing a terabyte of genuinely live latency-bound memory for hours, costing roughly $60000 monthly, which prices fakes out of the vote.
